bloodMarkers.target: Use the lab's own range. Low or suppressed TSH with high free T4/T3 fits overt hyperthyroidism; low TSH with normal free T4/T3 is subclinical. TSH can stay suppressed for several months after treatment starts, so it is a poor early marker

waterMl.notes: No change from FitPlate general water target; no hyperthyroid-specific fluid number found. Overactive thyroid raises body heat and sweating, so the general hot-weather, exercise and fever rules apply, but the app never pushes a target above the general cap. Fever with confusion or very fast heartbeat is an emergency, not a hydration problem. With heart, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or diuretics, show only the general range. Follow your doctor's advice.

warnings: General information, not medical advice. FitPlate does not diagnose hyperthyroidism; a doctor's examination and blood tests are needed.
The app never suggests starting, stopping, skipping or changing carbimazole, methimazole, PTU, beta-blockers or any thyroid treatment. Follow your doctor.
Emergency: fever with very fast heartbeat, agitation, confusion, vomiting or collapse in someone with overactive thyroid may be thyroid storm. Seek emergency care now (112).
Fever, sore throat or mouth ulcers while on antithyroid drugs: possible low white cells. Get urgent medical care; the doctor decides about the tablet.
Yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or abdominal pain on antithyroid drugs: contact the doctor the same day.
Do not take iodine, kelp or seaweed supplements or 'thyroid support' pills without a doctor; the ATA advises against iodine or kelp supplements above 500 µg/day; NIH upper limit is 1,100 µg/day.
A low-iodine diet before radioiodine is short and specific and is given by the doctor or hospital; the app does not create one.
Selenium supplements: doctor-led only (trial use in mild Graves' orbitopathy); upper limit 400 µg/day from all sources (NIH); do not self-start.
High-dose biotin can distort thyroid blood tests and imitate Graves' disease; tell your doctor and lab.
Caffeine can worsen palpitations, tremor and anxiety; no numeric limit found.
Weight commonly rises about 5-6 kg after treatment (UK cohorts); plan gently, no crash diets.
Smoking raises the risk and severity of Graves' eye disease; ask for quit support.
Drink more in heat per the general rules but never push a higher target; with heart, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or diuretics, follow your doctor's advice.

requires_doctor_input is true because overactive thyroid needs a doctor-set diagnosis, monitoring and treatment, drug side effects and thyroid storm are urgent, and pregnancy changes drug choice and iodine needs.
